name: honeymontana-creator-led
description: Talking-head + screen-demo style calibrated from a breakdown of the Honey Montana YouTube channel: the presenter is the stable visual anchor, cutaways (screen recordings, memes, reaction inserts) punctuate rather than replace them. Use for projects with an actual face-to-camera recording (not pure voiceover). Copy this file per channel/series instead of editing it in place.

narrative_arc.notes: Cut when the video switches between 'host talking', 'proof on screen', and 'reaction' — not on a fixed rhythm. For interview/podcast-length content, repeat 'deeper_walkthrough' as a longer loop instead of forcing the whole arc into one pass. Every mode switch should answer: does my face or the evidence convince the viewer more right now?

pacing.variable_pacing_rule: Slow down for anything the viewer must actually read or process (code, screen demos, comparisons) — a code screen can legitimately hold 10-30s. Speed up hard for punchlines/memes/reactions. Don't apply one uniform cut rhythm across both.

composition.rule_of_one: The host's face is the default state to return to; every cutaway should have an obvious reason to leave it and a natural point to cut back.

visual_language.attention: The host's face is the primary focal point by default; screen UI becomes primary only during an evidence beat, with an overlay label as the secondary read. See references/cinematic_principles.md system 1.
visual_language.depth: Real camera depth where available (workspace foreground objects, over-the-shoulder framing) — this profile has actual footage to work with, not just collage layering. See system 2.
visual_language.light: Favor footage that already separates the host from the background (practical/window light, warm key) — the color.grade_cdl nudge supports good source lighting, it doesn't fix bad separation. See system 3.
visual_language.tactility: Screen recordings should stay crisp/legible (no added grain); workspace/lifestyle b-roll can carry its own natural texture.

color.accent_usage: No single graphic accent color system — identity comes from the recurring face, workspace, and UI textures instead. Keep grading consistent across A-roll sessions so cuts back to the host don't jump in color temperature.
color.notes: A small warm nudge (slight red lift / blue pull in offset) plus a touch more saturation than neutral — meant to flatter skin tones and warm up room lighting without fighting the naturally cool light of monitors/UI in frame. Nudge by eye against a real render; this is a starting point, not a fixed look.

camera_motion.avoid: Don't animate the host cam itself beyond the punch-in — physical-feeling handheld moves undercut the 'stable anchor' role the face is playing.

transitions.rule: Switch information MODE (host / proof / reaction) rather than cutting for rhythm alone. A-roll-to-screen and screen-to-A-roll should be hard cuts; punch-ins are for emphasis within a single mode.

captions.style_notes: Utility captions, not a graphic centerpiece: short bold caption, highlight one word at most, arrows/circles around UI controls being discussed, a label over language/tool names, rating or yes/no markers for comparisons/tier lists.

sound_design.foley: Whatever the source recording actually carries (keyboard clatter, desk sounds) — keep it, don't add fabricated foley on top of real production audio.
sound_design.ambience: Keep the host's room tone consistent across cuts so switching between A-roll takes doesn't create an audible jump; workspace/lifestyle b-roll can carry its own ambience.

music_bed.role: sits lower under A-roll, even lower under screen tutorials; near-silent during interview/podcast segments
music_bed.ducking: lower under narration — see references/beat_plan_schema.md music_bed field

sound_design.silence: Let a genuinely strong on-camera line land with just room tone under it before cutting to the next beat — don't rush a reaction with a sound effect.
